name: Gallbladder surgery (cholecystectomy)
summary: How expats navigate gallbladder disease and laparoscopic cholecystectomy in Singapore — biliary colic vs infection, elective timing around travel, and diet expectations after surgery.
body:
Gallstones often announce themselves as night pain after rich meals. Workup usually starts with ultrasound and bloods; surgery (typically laparoscopic cholecystectomy) is the durable fix for symptomatic stones. Not every stone on a scan needs immediate removal — timing depends on symptoms and complications.

## When surgery moves sooner
- Recurrent biliary colic disrupting work/sleep
- Cholecystitis, cholangitis, or pancreatitis pathways
- Failed medical observation with escalating attacks
- Travel plans that make emergency care risky mid-flare

Emergency presentations go through A&E; elective lists sit with general surgery/hepatobiliary teams.

## Recovery and diet
Most people go home quickly after uncomplicated laparoscopy, but fat-tolerance varies for weeks. Ask about drain use, wound care in humidity, and when you can fly. Insurance pre-auth for elective cases needs precise diagnosis codes.

## How to choose
Prefer surgeons who explain open-conversion risk, bile-duct injury counselling, and stone-in-CBD strategies (MRCP/ERCP sequencing). Bring prior overseas ultrasounds. Be sceptical of “cleanse” packages sold instead of surgical assessment for true colic.

## Practical tip
Keep a symptom diary (timing vs meals). If pain radiates with fever/jaundice, do not wait for an elective clinic slot.
